implementation_notes: The hand-rolled 'link struct + registry' structure collapses into framework primitives: ASP.NET Core's LinkGenerator (injected via DI) produces the href with GetUriByAction/GetPathByName from an endpoint address plus route values, a small record Link(Href, Rel, Method) serialized with System.Text.Json serves as the carrier envelope, and the consumer dereferences with System.Uri (typed scheme/host/path access) and HttpClient — ideally an IHttpClientFactory-managed client. The link envelope itself has no single built-in type, so the tiny Link record stays hand-written; the classic fully manual form (own URL builder + registry) is still justified outside ASP.NET Core — console workers, message-queue consumers, or client apps that receive links and resolve them with HttpClient and Uri.TryCreate.
pitfalls: GetUriByAction/GetUriByName return string? and yield null when the route values bind to no endpoint; href! hides the failure and ships a dead link — fail at production time instead. Absolute-URI overloads take scheme+host, and Microsoft's own docs warn that trusting the request's Host lets untrusted input influence the generated URI: behind a proxy, emitted links can carry internal hostnames or attacker-controlled authorities, leaking topology to clients.

Dereferencing with 'new HttpClient()' per link exhausts sockets (TIME_WAIT buildup) because disposed clients keep their underlying HttpConnections open; use IHttpClientFactory so handler lifetime is pooled.

System.Uri.ToString() returns a canonically unescaped, human-friendly form while AbsoluteUri preserves percent-encodings — persisting or signing ToString() output can silently alter the href; Uri equality also unescapes, so two different hrefs may compare equal in dictionary-keyed link caches.

Serializing links as bare strings loses rel/method metadata, forcing consumers to guess whether a link is safe to mutate; keep a Dictionary<string, Link> (rel-keyed record with Href/Method) in the carrier payload so the contract survives System.Text.Json.
